public_rationale: The core claim is that OpenAI has no path to profitability. No deadline was given. Needing more cash is presented as a consequence. On 27 February 2026, OpenAI said it was raising $110 billion in a new funding round (e2). That matches the stated consequence, but a fundraise does not test the 'no path' claim. A 16 June 2026 report on leaked 2025 statements gives an operating loss of $20.92 billion for 2025, up from $8.78 billion in 2024 (e1). The same report says OpenAI is aiming for profitability by 2030 (e1). Continued losses fit the claim but do not show that profit cannot be reached. A stated target does not show that it will be reached. The evidence in this case does not show a full year of profit, which would contradict the claim. It also does not show OpenAI ceasing operations or being sold or restructured because it cannot fund its losses, which would support it.
limitations: The 2025 figures come from leaked statements as reported in the press, not from a public filing.
The evidence covers only 2025 results and one February 2026 funding announcement. It does not cover 2026 results.
'No path to profitability' is partly a judgment, and OpenAI's own profitability target of 2030 falls after the evaluation date.

criteria.contradiction_condition: OpenAI reports sustained profitability (positive net income or operating profit) in reliable financial statements.
